title: DC-area forecast: Strong midday storms today as heat continues through Friday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Storms continue moving through the DC region from north to south through around 3:30 p.m. Heavy rain, lightning, and gusty wind last for around 30 to 60 minutes for any given location.

What’s next? Very hot and humid tomorrow with highs in the mid-90s, the heat index up to 100 to 105, and a chance for late-day storms. Only slightly cooler Friday with more showers and storms possible, then looking like a pretty nice Labor Day weekend.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: Not quite as hot as Tuesday, but still steamier than most of us would prefer for early September. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Wednesday): A line of strong to severe storms comes through from north to south early to midafternoon. Temperatures drop to the 70s where storms come through. Otherwise it‘s cloudier with a touch cooler highs in the mid-80s to near 90 north and east of the Beltway, versus sunnier and hotter highs around 90 to 95 from near the Beltway to the south and west. High humidity everywhere (dew points in the low 70s) makes it feel several degrees warmer. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: A few more showers and strong storms are possible during the evening. Any storm that develops has some potential for damaging winds. Muggy evening 80s dip to overnight lows in the low to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): The cool front retreats to the northeast, likely leaving the entire region partly to mostly sunny and hot. Highs should reach the mid-90s with heat indexes rising to around 100 to 105. Scattered strong to severe storms are possible in the late afternoon or evening. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: After the chance of scattered strong to severe storms in the evening, skies are partly to mostly cloudy overnight with lows in the low to mid-70s and still humid. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Temperatures only come down slightly Friday with highs near 90 to the low 90s. Humidity stays up, and it's one more day with potential for scattered showers and storms as a front lingers nearby. Rain chances may continue into Friday evening but should diminish overnight. Humidity should also start to decline overnight with lows in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Low-Medium

The forecast is an encouraging one for Labor Day weekend. Can't rule out a shower south or west of DC on Saturday. But overall we should be partly to mostly sunny, mostly dry, and less humid Saturday through Monday. Highs in the low to mid-80s Saturday trend a little cooler Sunday and Monday, when highs top out in the upper 70s to mid-80s. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 2

Blistering late-season heat in 1980 sent temperatures to 101 degrees, part of a record-setting stretch of 90-degree days that extended deep into September.
